title: Retrospective Analysis of Elective Nodal Pelvic Radiotherapy With or Without Androgen Deprivation Therapy in Patients With PSMA PET/CT- Detected Pelvic Nodal Recurrence of Prostate Cancer
summary:
Background and Objective
In patients with prostate cancer and a relapse in the pelvic lymph nodes, radiotherapy is a central component of treatment. In recent years, these lymph nodes can be detected much more accurately and at an earlier stage by means of a modern imaging technique (PSMA PET/CT).

The aim of this study is to investigate the outcomes of treatment. Specifically, the entire lymphatic system of the pelvis is irradiated (so-called elective nodal pelvic radiotherapy) in order to treat the cancer with curative intent. This radiotherapy is administered either alone or in combination with hormonal therapy (androgen deprivation therapy).

This is a single-arm, retrospective cohort study at a single centre (LMU Klinikum). This means:

Data from patients who were treated as part of routine clinical care are analysed retrospectively.
There is no additional control group or additional interventions.
No additional doctor visits, examinations, or radiation exposure are required for participation in the project.
The study evaluates how effective the treatment is based on the following criteria:

Biochemical progression-free survival: How long does the cancer marker (PSA) remain low without the disease progressing?
Overall survival: How long do the patients survive overall?
PSA response: How does the PSA level respond to the treatment?
Side effects: What treatment-related side effects occur?
Additional Project: Artificial Intelligence (AI) A sub-project focuses on the development of an artificial intelligence model (deep learning). This model is intended to be able to automatically outline the affected lymph nodes in the PSMA PET/CT images (autosegmentation) and to generate the necessary radiation fields from them.
conditions: Secondary and unspecified malignant neoplasm: Intrapelvic lymph nodes

interventions.name: Patients with PSMA PET/CT detected pelvic-confined nodal recurrence of prostate cancer treated at LMU Klinikum

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Histologically confirmed adenocarcinoma of the prostate.
Biochemical and/or clinical recurrence following primary curative•intent treatment (radical prostatectomy and/or definitive radiotherapy)
PSMA PET/CT demonstratingoneormore PSMA-avid lesion(s) confined tothepelvic lymphnode region.
No evidence of extrapelvic nodal, bone, or visceral metastatic disease at the time of recurrence,
Treatment With elective nodal pelvic radiotherapy (ENRT), With or Without concomitant/adjuvant androgen deprivation therapy or Other hormonal therapy
Exclusion criteria:
No histological confirmation of Prostate cancer.
Evidenceof extrapelvic nodal, bone. orvisceral metastatic disease atthe time of recurrence.
Incomplete medical records precluding evaluation of the relevant treatment or follow-up data.
